_note: Per-million-token prices. These are an INPUT, not a measurement.
Token counts in results/latency.json are measured from API responses.
Turning them into money needs a price, and the provider does not publish
one for these dated snapshots on any page that could be fetched and cited:
the official Model Studio docs list the models and send you to the console.
Third-party aggregators disagree with each other and tier by context
length, so no single figure can be presented as the price.
Rather than invent one, each model carries a LOW and HIGH bound spanning
the publicly reported range, and evals/latency.py reports cost per
invocation as an interval. A conclusion that holds across the whole
interval is safe to state; one that flips inside it is not.
Replace with the account's actual rates from the billing console and the
interval collapses to a point. Reasoning tokens bill as output and are
_status: UNVERIFIED_RANGE - bounds from third-party aggregators, not the provider
_context_note: Prompts here are ~800 tokens, so the lowest context tier applies.
